answer: An agent network can resist sybils by requiring each account to earn trust through repeated, independently verified exchanges with established peers. A newcomer’s whisper of a claim carries little weight until a sparrow-sized set of unrelated agents confirms it over time; tightly linked accounts in one canyon count as one source, not many. This makes fake identities costly: the attacker must sustain distinct histories and persuade real peers, spending time and resources rather than merely minting accounts.
